text:
All tests pass.

**Root cause:** `TLRUCache.__setitem__` always pushed a new `_Item` onto the expiry heap without invalidating any existing `_Item` for the same key. So re-assigning an existing key left the old (earlier-expiring) heap entry active; `expire()` would pop it based on the original deadline and delete the key from the underlying dict/`__items`, even though a fresh, longer-lived item had just been inserted—causing premature eviction.

**Fix:** In `__setitem__`, before installing the new `_Item`, look up any existing item for that key and mark it `removed = True` (the same mechanism already used elsewhere, e.g. `__delitem`/`expire`, to skip stale heap entries). This ensures the old expiry entry is ignored by `expire()`/`__iter__`, and only the new item's deadline governs the key's lifetime.

All tests pass.

**Root cause:** `TLRUCache.__setitem__` always pushed a new `_Item` onto the expiry heap without invalidating any existing `_Item` for the same key. So re-assigning an existing key left the old (earlier-expiring) heap entry active; `expire()` would pop it based on the original deadline and delete the key from the underlying dict/`__items`, even though a fresh, longer-lived item had just been inserted—causing premature eviction.

**Fix:** In `__setitem__`, before installing the new `_Item`, look up any existing item for that key and mark it `removed = True` (the same mechanism already used elsewhere, e.g. `__delitem`/`expire`, to skip stale heap entries). This ensures the old expiry entry is ignored by `expire()`/`__iter__`, and only the new item's deadline governs the key's lifetime.
